claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 20 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 20 years old, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether he is still in approved education or training. Child Benefit usually stops when a child turns 16, but can continue until their 20th birthday if they remain in eligible full-time education or approved training.

Could you tell me if Alex is currently in any of the following:
- Full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar qualifications)?
- An approved training course (such as a traineeship in England)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished his studies a while back.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Unfortunately, based on what you've told me, it appears you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. Child Benefit is only available for children who are either:

- Under 16 years old, or
- Under 20 years old **and** still in approved full-time education or training

Since Alex is 20 years old and is no longer in education or training, he doesn't meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

Let me confirm this decision for you now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the official guidance, I can now confirm my assessment. The rules clearly state that you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16, and if your child is 16 or over, you'll normally still qualify only if they are under 20 **and** stay in approved education or training.

Since Alex is 20 years old and is not in any approved education or training, he does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I've completed my assessment of your eligibility for Child Benefit.

**Decision: Not Eligible**

**For Alex:** Unfortunately, you are not eligible for Child Benefit. The rules state that Child Benefit can only be claimed for:
- Children under 16 years old, or
- Young people aged 16 to 19 who are still in approved education or training

Since Alex is 20 years old and no longer in education or training, he does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

I'm sorry I couldn't bring you better news. If your circumstances change, or if you have any other children you'd like to ask about, please feel free to reach out. If you believe there are special circumstances that might apply to your situation, you can also contact the Child Benefit Office directly for further guidance.
